nodes.label: The Spectra Compendium
nodes.rationale: Extracted verbatim from the restore-point-2_13 bank (694 files, register max R 1700, certificate 1.8.3) and declared stale if the bank advances past 2_13 - the index carries the answers while the Register carries the working record.

nodes.label: The Quantum Defect
nodes.rationale: E = -Z_c^2 R/(n-d)^2, so a channel's whole Rydberg series follows from one number and the core charge - which is why one cell can stand for a series.

nodes.label: The Stored Defect Is the Median
nodes.rationale: Measured, not chosen: of 433 series whose member count reproduces exactly from raw, the stored value equals the median in 430 (99.3%), and the 18 mean-agreements distinguish nothing. Mean and asymptotic perspectives are carried alongside as perspectives of one definition (T6, M's ruling).

nodes.label: The Three Grades - exact, measured, computed
nodes.rationale: Nothing is ungraded: a value with no provenance is not a coordinate. 929 exact, 358 measured, 103,545 computed.

nodes.label: The Witness - 358 of 104,832 cells
nodes.rationale: Register 1578 replaced VERIFIED/POSSIBLE/IMPROBABLE grading because improbable is a judgement about the future, not a fact about the record, and register 1287 had already ruled that an index mixing OBJECT with OBSERVER cannot close. 0.341% of the index has been checked against reality.

nodes.label: The Bounds on the Unwitnessed
nodes.rationale: Named obstacles, not probabilities. The charge bound is the one to distrust - it reads 'no analysis located', not 'no analysis exists', and register 1577 found twelve MEASURED cells above it in this index's own file.

nodes.label: The Channel Equation (the filler)
nodes.rationale: Domain Z <= 92, charge <= 10, l <= 4, single-parent core; fitted on 277 channels at rms 0.1329, R^2 0.9747, anchored at Z = 2 and Z = 90. Every value outside the domain is marked improbable.

nodes.label: Multiplicity Is Not a Free Coordinate
nodes.rationale: Hund's first rule on the core's ground configuration gives the allowed values, exact on all 24 electron counts tested; applying it as a constraint removes 247,248 cells - 71% of the naive product.

nodes.label: The Parent-Term Wall
nodes.rationale: A closed-shell core gives one series per l; an open-shell core gives one per parent, interleaved and converging on different limits. That is why the compendium holds Ne-like and Na-like ions at charge 15-16 and no open-shell ion above charge 6 - an open-shell core does not produce the object a quantum-defect index holds.

nodes.label: The Janet Collapse
nodes.rationale: The collapse coordinate is read from the periodic table, not fitted, which is why a defect at l = 2 can be large in one element and negligible in its neighbour.

nodes.label: The Isoelectronic Ladder
nodes.rationale: A is fixed rather than fitted: as charge grows at constant electron count the core collapses to a point and the ion becomes hydrogenic, so d -> 0. That is the periodic table's own edge, and setting A = 0 leaves one parameter.

nodes.label: A Channel Is a Curve
nodes.rationale: The sign of d2 names the regime - positive for core penetration, negative for core polarisation. The sign rule is NIST's own; what the compendium adds is the measurement across 274 channels and the finding that |d2| predicts scatter at R^2 = 0.761.

nodes.label: The La/Ce Capture Group
nodes.rationale: La/Ce is the group that earns its place: the other three fill coordinate space, La/Ce is where the filling order itself breaks, and holding it in the index lets the anomaly be stated as a coordinate fact rather than a footnote.
